blocks.text: For SFO–Bangkok on January 15, the main choice is whether reaching Bangkok the prior local night is worth a longer elapsed journey, or whether to leave later and arrive the next day. The award options below are single-award journeys; their points quotes are all in Aeroplan, so they can be compared within that program.

If arriving earliest matters, the Hong Kong routing reaches Bangkok at 10:25 p.m. on January 16. It leaves SFO at 11:45 a.m. on January 15 and takes 19 hours 40 minutes—so the earlier arrival comes with a substantially earlier start than the late-night departure option.

A different compromise is the Taipei routing: leave SFO at noon and arrive at 1:25 a.m. on January 17, after 22 hours 25 minutes. That is 3 hours later than the Hong Kong option’s arrival, but the SFO departure is 15 minutes later; it also gives you a distinct routing choice rather than another near-identical schedule.
Later departure via Taipei, arriving just after midnight.
blocks.label: Taipei routing

blocks.text: If you prefer a late departure and the shortest elapsed time among these choices, the other Hong Kong option leaves at 11:15 p.m. on January 15 and arrives at 9:50 a.m. on January 17 in 19 hours 35 minutes. Its shorter elapsed duration does not mean the earlier arrival: it reaches Bangkok 11 hours 25 minutes after the prior-evening option.
Shortest elapsed-time choice here, with a next-morning arrival.
blocks.label: Late departure, next-morning arrival

blocks.text: For context, the endpoint-pair cash search also returned a one-traveler SFO–Bangkok itinerary for $440 USD, departing at 9:40 a.m. January 15 and arriving at 8:25 a.m. January 17 after 31 hours 45 minutes. Its reported price scope is unknown, so it is not a confirmed party total or a directly equivalent award comparison.
